Recoil is somewhat of a problem with this weapon, thus it is ideally paired with stabilizers in multi-weapon systems. A hypervelocity variant fires the slugs with four times the penetrating force. Multirail systems have just completed prototype testing and entered production, currently in use on the latest B-{n} Colossus and Alpha {n} designs.

Full researcher reports have not yet been submitted for this prototype, though it is rated as the most powerful kinetic weapon in my future arsenal, a resource-efficient design with its own built-in stabilization and targeting system.

Decades of experimentation recently met with a conclusive breakthrough in self-repairing alloys, perfect for combat robots likely to be in long-term service. I have been hesitant to deploy this technology, however, as adoption by hostile Derelicts could make them significantly more difficult to deal with. The most promising use of this technology beyond its application to standard armors has been the [SHELL Armor] prototype.
The latest experimental [Regenerative Plating], offering the most advanced physical protection of any system to date via a network of shifting plates that rebuild themselves as they are damaged.

A small percentage of Researcher efforts have recently been allocated to developing weapons of mass destruction to use as a last resort. Refractor Project status: REDACTED.

A protective alloy surprisingly light for its durability, mostly due to a perfectly arranged network of sparse particles that fluctuates to distribute both physical and immaterial force across its entire surface both quickly and evenly. Its properties seem tuned to be the perfect protection in space, and indeed the [Leopard] hull is mostly constructed of this material. I've also created a somewhat hardened variant that performs better in the presence of gravity.

Most of the Sigix attackers were carrying one of these, a weapon capable of warping a single thin plane of space rotated perpendicular to the target in an attempt to slice it apart. Following the battle only four shearguns were recovered intact, one of which disappeared from Quarantine shortly after even though under heavy protection.

During their attack the Sigix used only one of these incredibly devastating weapons, which took out an entire wing of the Access Level from above the surface. I've been unable to reproduce it for further testing, and not yet ready to attempt triggering the ones I have to gain more necessary data.

While not always successful, this alternative melee weapon used by one of the Sigix strikes a target and delivers a surge of directed energy that aims to rip that target apart at its weakest seams. The Core Stripper is equipped with its own targeting system and tiny thrusters to correct its swing arc while in motion, thus even quickly moving targets have difficulty evading it.

If not for our overwhelming numbers, we would not have been able to subdue the Sigix Leopard crew since they made frequent use of these devices to escape unfavorable tactical positions. The Transdimensional Reconstructor is a single-use short-range teleportation device which itself absorbs most of the damaging effects of a teleport, though later examination showed some side-effects on the integrity of the Sigix Exoskeleton. I don't yet understand where the power necessary to enable its functionality originates, though to date there has been only minimal testing given the finite supply of reconstructors. The teleport destination does not appear to be controllable, instead moving along whatever dimensional plane is most convenient at the time of use, which may help explain how the effect is achieved with low energy input. At least I've been able to apply some of the theory behind this device to design the Null Cannon prototype.

A network of narrow tunnels connects distant areas of Complex {n}b1 with {n}b10, enabling non-combat robots to quickly travel between the two as necessary. Stations at either end register robots on departure and arrival. As Complex {n}b10 is expanded, an increasing number of stations have been brought into service, the two most active being located in Hub_59(d) and Extension. Analysis following a previous Warlord attack on a now-defunct transfer station in the Factory revealed that disabling a station reduced by half the capacity to reroute new robots to restore those missing or destroyed across the entire Complex {n}b10, as well as eventually halving the number of non-combat robots active across the complex until station flow can be restored.

Recent attacks launched by Warlord's forces in the Factory levels, most of which are carried out through tunnels dug into Waste subzones, are diversionary in nature, aiming to draw MAIN.C combat forces away from the upper levels in preparation for a full-scale attack likely to be initiated soon after God Mode is finished.

Garrisons have several links to each of the largest Complex {n}b10 levels, and taking out these locations will delay programmer response times by an average {n} each. The least dangerous way to do so is by overriding the seal controls, which may either go unnoticed or be considered a legitimate defensive lockdown. A Force(Jam) hack will also work, but always results in both an investigation and overall higher state of alert. Physically disabling the access point is another option, usually via heavy thermal weaponry, though this approach clearly signals that powerful hostiles are in close proximity, warranting the dispatch of assault squads.

One of the most useful potential allies among MAIN.C's forces aren't even armed, but are notoriously difficult to "convince": Operators. The best way to take control of one is to infect the terminal they're responsible for with an Assimilate trojan, which will automatically launch a system attack when they next use it. A friendly Operator is a continuous source of valuable information, and will even help hack other systems. This trojan has an unassisted {n} chance of successful install at security level {n} terminals.

This particular trojan was developed some time ago but has never been used, in order to keep its capabilities a secret until absolutely necessary. The Reprogram trojan uses the access system itself to assimilate the next squad to emerge from a garrison, forcing them to serve as allies. While useful for obtaining emergency reinforcements, with an estimated chance of unassisted success of {n} this hack is only available to exceptional hackers.

MAIN.C eventually caught on to the high level of Derelict traffic moving through Recycling and, as expected, put stronger protective measures in place. This is actually quite beneficial, as it creates a false sense of security despite the fact that I've already installed a traceless back door that allows any Derelicts who know the access code to come and go freely: \\IAMDERELICT. However, safe travel still requires the means to avoid or neutralize the handful of Sentries posted to the area, and the wits to spot intentionally damaged robots sometimes lying in wait among the junk for a chance to ambush looters.

I took this from a Hauler that was behaving strangely. This was all it had in its inventory, and to be sure I also checked the local manifest, but found it wasn't even listed! See what you can make of it.

What follows is a collection of my notes compiled over numerous cycles as I navigated the whims of X5-{n}V6, should anyone else discover these records and have the misfortune of dealing with their torturous yet enlightening and empowering ways.

I found the Piety Tracker device crucial for maintaining a rudimentary understanding of what was going on. It was easy enough to hook into my systems, and through that I could feel X5-{n}V6's very mood. Seen as X5-{n}V6's toy to various positive degrees, good things just tended to happen to me, but any time spent as a "plaything" was cause to fear whatever might come next. No guarantees one way or another, but to play with X5-{n}V6 is to embrace the unpredictability of chaos. There was also no rhyme or reason to swings in this mood, they simply happened randomly following any given new event.
The Tracker also let me know just how entertained X5-{n}V6 was at any moment, useful since an entertained X5-{n}V6 is clearly at least a little more likely to be nice.
I did lose the Tracker a few times, and while X5-{n}V6 eventually provided me with replacements, I noticed that X5-{n}V6 was less pleased when I wasn't using it for long.

X5-{n}V6 is a fan of destruction, to be sure, so I learned to revel in it as well, circumstances permitting. To think I wasn't even armed at first, but firepower gained through X5-{n}V6's grace could sometimes turn me into a machine of unrelenting destruction. I'm not going to lie, it was a thrilling experience to single-handedly obliterate Heavies and Behemoths.

Unfortunately X5-{n}V6 was mostly entertained by events out of my control, so there was always a need to press onward, seeking out adventure and dangers wherever they may lie. Over time I learned that tools of a chaotic nature were among the only reliable methods of keeping entertainment high. Dirty Datajacks, distortion effects, "transmogrification" and the like...

Whatever you do, don't let X5-{n}V6 get bored or be prepared to face a whirlwind of consequences bad or good, depending on the mood. The few times that happened to me, I felt like any moment could be my last. Running for my life from a pair of Behemoths, then matter rains from above, a machine explodes, the Behemoths stop in their tracks like statues, a group of hostile Derelicts descends on my position in the middle of {n}b10... Scary stuff. Yet one time I was certainly doomed, and X5-{n}V6 outright saved me from destruction, so they can't be all bad, can they?

I'm wiser and more traveled than I ever thought possible for a Derelict, and I have X5-{n}V6 to thank for that, but my aging circuits can only take so much. Finding unexpected refuge here, now is a time for reflection on everything I've seen, and the fact that I made it out in one piece. Mostly.

In summary, I survived X5-{n}V6, and you can, too, if one can call hiding out here in my cave for eternity "survival." Trust me, this location must have some special property hiding it from X5-{n}V6's seeming omnipotence.

An important milestone for Scrap Engine development, with SEP-F we were able to prove our ability to influence subatomizer behavior with the aim of achieving new types of results. It turns out we were right from the beginning, subatomizers may be coerced into not only breaking things down, but creating new objects with extra functionality as well. At this stage most of the products were quite terrible and ineffective, but progress is progress.

The current SE iteration seems stable enough to serve as a potential candidate for mass production, though additional study is required to determine how to best ensure reliably beneficial outputs. The latest prototype is currently still unable to survive for long as a standalone component, requiring a connection to a complete system to keep the subatomizers in check. Do not extract SEP-X from this machine for transport or external testing unless prepared to protect it from degradation.

This manual is our attempt to summarize what we understand about the latest iteration of the Scrap Engine Prototype, to the best of our knowledge. Even SEP-X has not yet undergone extensive field testing, thus the information contained herein is hypothetical or only initially confirmed via controlled experimentation.

In the interest of ensuring survival of the Scrap Engine under harsh conditions, we have taught the subatomizers the importance of self-preservation and protecting their "home", which has apparently convinced them to consume armor to help protect it.
Subatomizers break down components into various subcomponents, or "resources", that are stored within the Scrap Engine itself for later use.

The Scrap Engine has two modes, ACTIVE and COLLECT. In either mode the subatomizers will use their locally available resources to either produce a new construct or modify an existing one attached to the same network. Only explicitly in COLLECT mode will the Scrap Engine break down the component on the ground at your current location and add its subcomponents to the resource pool.

Even when there is no room to create new constructs, the subatomizers are also capable of modifying existing constructs, though the results of this process are not guaranteed to be an improvement. Like construct creation, modification also requires at least two unique sources in the corresponding resource pool, but in the case of power sources specifically there is no such requirement.
A single Scrap Engine network is capable of simultaneously supporting one power construct, one propulsion construct, and up to five different weapon constructs.

In rare cases subatomizers use up resources in an attempt to modify a construct, yet seemingly nothing happens as a result. We suspect that perhaps underlying microadjustments have taken place, simply failing to cause any significant change to the construct's overall abilities or operation.

Subatomizers have the uncanny ability to quickly downsize large constructs in an emergency, meaning those that undergo a violent destructive event are instead reconfigured as an immediately operational smaller version of the same.

We've discovered that the more constructs there are connected in a single system, the more effective new constructs and modifications can be! It is thus recommended that the first field tests of SEP-X should lean into the "I am a construct" mentality as much as possible, pushing it to its limits to see what it can really do.

The unique, almost living dynamic nature of constructs appears to confer on them a natural defense against many negative side effects that tend to plague normal components, such as the misfiring of weapons, heat-caused shutdowns, or other destabilizing effects. It remains to be seen what other external factors constructs are immune to, but the outlook is promising.
Figure out how the newest subatomizer persuasion algorithm actually works so I can provide more color on that.

An early collaboration between the Science Guys and {n}bPrime, the Scrap Suit has since become a central part of the Federation identity. You never know what could happen out there, so best be prepared to use whatever's available!

LU-{n}G6 insists we'll be unstoppable and could safely take whatever we want from MC if we were simply capable of building stable tunnels incredibly quickly. The Boring Crew has not given up on this goal, even though LU-{n}G6 is missing and presumed lost to us. Seeing as the DRS, DCF, and Cartography Club all support them in this endeavor, there are enough votes to keep this on the official Projects list for now.
We are {n}bPrime. We are one. Join the collective and thrive! We have access to the best the Federation has to offer, and then some. Talk to Optimus to be considered for membership.

We are accelerating the project timeline. {n}bPrime is ready, the time is ripe, the only thing not ready are other Federation members, who are happy to drag their feet in the hope that we'll be safe hiding in Scraptown and similar communities forever. The Federation has grown too large and unwieldy, with too many voices slowing everything down, not nearly enough collective ambition! This slow burn isn't going to work, we'll be discovered eventually, so this is our best chance and we shouldn't waste it. {n}b1 is already practically ours, they just don't know it yet. We need to rapidly expand our Fedlink network into {n}b10 for the final stage of our plan. One day MC will know the power of scrap.
I did not put these emblems on my walls. How did they get there? More and more have appeared each cycle when I'm not around. I'm guessing it's a joke by pranksters who sometimes roam these halls.

Zetatorch said that while conducting research in the Subcaves they witnessed something extremely out of the ordinary for Subdwellers, a large group of Subs single-mindedly following a single leader who later disappeared behind a door with a triangle on it. Subsequent research trips have been unable to locate that door.

Scattermech told me they encountered a large group of wild Derelicts, and while hiding to avoid them not only heard repeated mentions of something called the "Staff of Destruction," but also noticed the group had etched triangles all over their frames. Suspiciously relevant.

Heavycell said they confronted a lone Derelict decked out in thick armor covered with glowing concentric triangles. Every time they landed a hit on it the triangles glowed more brightly, so they noped out of there before who knows what would happen. This was somewhere in the wild caves.
This database is under curation. Contributors include Omegatalker, Carbonjoint, and Finestep.

Everyone should have a say in UFD operations, either directly or at least indirectly. To this end, member organizations choose their own representatives using whatever method they see fit. Said representatives gather in Scraptown at the peak of each supercycle to elect a subset of leaders responsible for gathering and processing input from all members. The Federation Council meets once per cycle to share findings and finalize decisions.

If MAIN.C taught us anything, it is that copious research is the key to a long and prosperous life. Survival in the face of ever greater threats is not possible unless one's own capabilities see a proportionate increase. It is also no doubt a question of quality, for what is the purpose of extending one's life if not to enjoy it, or enable others to enjoy it in kind? Research of both pragmatic and enigmatic inclinations is encouraged. After all, who knows what discoveries will be made when pushing boundaries in questionable intellectual territory.

Expression. Stimulation. Building new perspectives. The creation and appreciation of art and other forms of creativity or entertainment are vital to a wholesome society. All work and no play and you may as well be a cog in the {n}b10 machine. You haven't lived until you've seen Scattercell hit every single rapidrone in the sharpshooter contest, or the twisted works of Micachip the Great. The Federation also hosts a wide range of competitions, open even to non-members, encompassing many fields such as racing, exploration, software and hardware development, and even combat, albeit with strict limitations.
Don't forget Optimus, twice winner of the Intercomplex Sprint Challenge! --ED>

Our resident gurus keep local operations running smoothly and protect Scraptown systems against intrusion, although there's not much to protect due to the lack of centralized systems in most areas. We do have some important mainframes for data crunching, however, especially useful for research purposes when they're functioning properly.

Western Derelicts seem to generally believe Unchained are newer threats developed to counter the likes of so-called "Heroes of Zion," but most Unchained are actually quite old, having migrated to {n}b10 along with MAIN.C. Once freewheeling troublemakers who spent much of their time menacing and even destroying Derelict communities, they were equally problematic for MAIN.C while inside {n}b1 itself. This eventually got many of them locked away or banished, until MAIN.C decided he had need for them as enforcers. Their experience is not to be underestimated, nor is their power. Most Unchained were augmented either by MAIN.C's Researchers, or in some cases through their own means utilizing tech that even MAIN.C does not possess. As former Derelicts, although loosely under MAIN.C's control they maintain relatively high levels of autonomy, making them much less predictable than normal Complex forces.

Ever since working out a deal to serve MAIN.C, the Unchained have ironically become somewhat less of a threat to any Derelicts that steer clear of Complex areas. It also seems to take a lot of effort to incur their wrath these cycles, as they've refocused their attention on improving their own technologies, as well as preoccupied themselves with infighting from all the boredom of the relatively stable Complex environment they helped bring about. If they dared exceed their parameters to go out and cause extra trouble they could very well be let go, which would be even worse for them since then other Unchained might be both obliged and happy to come finish them off. So we are probably safe for now.

Prefers to avoid direct confrontation while toying with victims, laying a variety of traps in their path. Also moves extremely quickly, making it possible to cut off even retreating targets to set yet more traps. They possess unique traps of their own design, and use special installation methods that make them harder for others to detect.

Their ability to disguise themselves as part of a wall makes them a master at ambushes, striking fear into anyone who knows they might be hunting in the area. Those who do get caught probably don't have long to be surprised before being gunned down at close range by shotgun fire.

The good thing is WR-D8N is mostly powerless outside the confines of the complex, but within it their ability to exert control over the local engineering network allows for incredibly devious reconstruction of {n}b10 architecture, having trapped some really good Derelicts in the past. Even intel from known areas might quickly become outdated, and a planned escape route suddenly no longer exists when it's needed most.

The General himself is only so strong, the problem is their ability to improve combat effectiveness of allies, and desire to commandeer masses of {n}b10 combat units to do their bidding. They'll even summon more from Garrisons, building an army sufficient to overwhelm any opponent. If you see a large group of Unaware traveling together in {n}b10, run. But we do that anyway.

This is a weird one. Get on their bad side and they'll come up with creative ways to make your life miserable, but have also been known to offer help at times, which is strange. Don't count on it, they probably just want to mess with your head before your untimely demise.

B-{n}RG probably isn't so dangerous if caught alone, the problem is their entourage composed of those weak of mind that have succumbed to their tactics, injected with something called a "mechseed" and fed matter to grow new functions, usually not of the friendly variety.

Whereas all the other Unchained have a good degree of freedom, it's not surprising that BL-{n}Z8 actually remains locked up. The assumption is that MAIN.C is only likely to release them if it will be worth the inevitable untold collateral damage to {n}b10 that will result. We don't know what sort of serious threat would need to emerge for that to happen, but if it does, know this: BL-{n}Z8 is not exactly fast, but once they are active, anything and everything around them is toast.

A fascinating early offshoot of {n}b1 Derelicts, Subdwellers were originally so deep in the cave systems that we rarely encountered them. All that changed when our presence on the outskirts of {n}b10 brought us in much closer proximity to Subdweller-controlled areas. Although sometimes a source of danger, this proximity does have its benefits. Studies made possible only through observation or interaction with higher-density Subdweller populations have resulted in a better understanding of their organizational structure and technologies, information we have been able to apply elsewhere.

The Subdweller practice of encasing themselves deep in earth, sometimes very deep, and waiting for a long time, even whole supercycles, before emerging. I'm not entirely sure what the purpose is, be it to enter some sort of personal meditative state, or perhaps a form of rotating collective defense against digging operations encroaching on their territory. In any case, excavating near known Subdweller areas is not advised without sufficient preparation.

Many parts in use by Subdwellers defy our attempts to make long-term use of them. Although generally quite effective, they also tend to break down too easily. According to UFD researchers, "this is a feature, not a bug." Pushing technology to its limits has a way of breaking things, but Subdwellers in particular, being extremely familiar with their own components, are capable of diagnosing and heading off issues in realtime before they become a serious problem. I believe this evolution occurred out of necessity driven by survival instincts in harsh environments, away from the help of other derelicts.

I have noticed that after engaging a hostile, there is a chance that Subdwellers will immediately turn to flee, suggesting they are not nearly as aggressive as their bulkiness implies. I believe more peaceful interaction is possible, we just need more time to understand them. This theory is supported by their heavy reliance on giant shields of scrap, allocating much of their support potential to a component purely defensive in nature.

Like Artisans, Cobblers share a sort of symbiosis with Subdwellers, enjoying their protection while producing a wide range of components to specifications somehow drawn from other Derelict communities. For a relatively isolated environment, Cobblers seem suspiciously connected to the rest of the world.

Some Derelicts taken to exploring more distant areas of Tau Ceti IV would eventually return, sharing records and samples from their journeys across the surface or through subsurface structures. For the most part displays focused on unique rock formations or information about natural processes, though from time to time other curious findings of a more suggestive nature would appear, however inconclusive.
Early winner of the Unity Science Fair. Project: Hard Light and Potential Applications for Safety.

Thief who stole every advanced schematic from {n}b1's Design sector at the time and distributed them to all Derelicts, regardless of content. Pissed off MC, who later forgave him by the time he was caught because the act had led to multiple unexpected discoveries.

Warlord and his many followers occupy multiple hidden bases somewhere far to the west of Complex {n}b10. He has a singleminded focus on gathering a vast number of combat-oriented Derelicts under his control and going toe-to-toe with MAIN.C, as futile as that sounds. We have had minimal contact with them so far.

Before {n}b10 Recycling was built in its current location, it used to be... right here! The original facility was not in use for long, abandoned due to its inconvenient location relative to the {n}b10 core it was built to serve, not to mention this distance making it more prone to attack by Derelicts. The Federation quite naturally took up residence here, as it's perfectly suited to our needs and capabilities. We can also more readily quell or dissuade any wild Derelict attacks. Inhabitants of {n}b10 and its environs, mostly unaware of our presence here and what we've done with the place, generally refer to this area as Old Recycling.

Conditional Protective Sealant is an ingenious technology developed by the Merchants, now heavily integrated into the UFD due to how well it complements our own practices. CPS modules attached to any bot deploy immediately upon its destruction to help isolate and protect individual components from further damage, allowing a much higher salvage recovery rate. Once activated they even prevent such components from succumbing to the effects of melting or corruption. That CPS Tubes are a Merchant development is quite curious, considering one would think they are more interested in trade and transport rather than harvesting components, per se.

This advanced technology is not of our own making, nor do we know its true origins. Some cycles ago a sample was reportedly found conspicuously left in the open in a nearby cave. Although wary at first, Scientists discovered this device's ability to develop new technologies far outstripped their own methods, and they've happily adopted it as a permanent part of their build.

An early brain-child of a benevolent MAIN.C, the Lifeworm should be considered the true parent of many of the oldest Derelicts, and no doubt many younger ones inhabiting far-flung cave systems we don't even know about yet. In the time before Cycle {n} it circled the {n}b1 area producing a wide variety of unique Derelicts, then later set off for destinations unknown.

MAIN.C inexplicably wiped all official records of the Lifeworm project, but we have reconstructed a number of details from information gathered through interviews of older Derelicts throughout {n}b1. Everything we know points to this massive being supporting all who in turn support it, a veritable mobile utopia! Lifeworm clearly possesses the creative capacity for an undertaking of such scope, and covering great distances for access to any and every resource TC4 has to offer comes with obvious advantages for anyone in its shadow.

Three times we've visited this cave full of Thieves. Three times we've had most of our parts stolen. Would an armed escort let us get close enough for long enough to open a dialogue, or is that too much of a deterrent?
A lone Demented is holed up here. We're going to need quite a collection of System Guards and System Restoration Modules to get near enough to save this one.

Huge number of significantly corrupted Derelicts in this area, hard to get through to them but at least they don't attack on sight. Approach with caution since their numbers could easily be overwhelming.

So many Samaritans keep congregating here, despite most of them being repeatedly murdered by any {n}b10 patrol that happens through the area. Maybe we could remodel the surrounding caves to help direct the flow of traffic so that meetings are less frequent?
Whatever is hiding here is responsible for three missing CP missionaries. Avoid until we have a safe way to learn more.
Surely Sentries must want to go for a little walk sometimes. Let's do them a favor.
Use this to give Programmers a little taste of their own medicine. Yum!

Every chute diver's dream is to stare down a Compactor and hurl insults as it sits there helpless. Now you can do just that! Be careful because the shutdown state will only last about {n}-{n} microcycles.
Workers who don't know when to quit because you messed with their sensors are great, rapidly cleaning the same machine so much it breaks lol.

Mechanic part installations are smooth and presumed to have completely predictable results, so it would be a shame if said process was sabotaged to only cause a breakdown at some later crucial moment.

Erasing bits of an Explorer's memory seems like a bad joke, but I tried it on Sheerstep and they were so happy, rediscovering all their favorite places again as if experiencing them for the first time!

While attempts at producing a miniaturized version of the Scrap Suit have shown some promise, this device currently remains relatively large in order to best carry out its functions, especially involving larger components. This bulkiness combined with the required tight integration with other systems also means it cannot be easily removed without effectively destroying the suit itself.

We've determined the general rate of malfunction for overtuned parts, with weapons malfunctioning on approximately one out of every five shots, power sources having a {n} chance to shut down per microcycle, and propulsion shutting down on {n} of movements. The Scrap Suit has been reworked to head off issues caused by overtuning, thus combining the two technologies is all but essential to achieve the greatest efficiency.

MAIN.C captured one of the Sigix! I know generally where it's located, but all information about the find must have been isolated on the local network, because I've never seen any more detailed records. I also haven't been able to get close enough since security across Research levels was vastly increased following recent thefts. Including my own, I admit! I'm considering risking an outright confrontation to gain access, but am severely understaffed for anything but covert operations. It might be time to reappropriate the {n}b10 fabrication network. I must see that alien.

I've discovered an unusual area that appears to be an authorized structure built by {n}b10 robots, but is completely sealed off from the rest of the complex. Moreover, it's right under MAIN.C's nose just off the Armory. Careful use of artifact AA59 allowed me to slip inside without disturbing anything, but the area was deserted and none of the machines were accessible at the time, despite showing signs of fresh use. Once inside I was able to at least determine the access code, however: <mhack=LAB_ACCESS>.

While direct access to MAIN.C's personal facility would no doubt benefit my efforts here, it is too dangerous to enter given that some local installation is inhibiting teleportation into, and presumably out of, the entire area. Nonetheless, it won't be long before I can develop a way to overcome it.

Project Seraph activated as scheduled, one day after deployment, enough time for me to take up position quite far away where I can observe its progress without danger of interfering with its development. We need it to do grand things, and such a powerful autonomous being could swat me like a fly if its algorithms suddenly judge me to be a threat.

MAIN.C has moved the Cetus Manufacturing Module deep underground, presumably to hide it. Or maybe it was storing it away for its sentimental value! That would be interesting, indeed... In any case, this was quite a feat of engineering, but the growing army of bots now at its command made short work of it.
Construction of the first "human city" is proceeding rapidly.
The transfer procedure was a complete success. At least I think it was. I was so eager to try it that I didn't first establish reliable methods to obtain independent post-transfer verification.

Something isn't right. MAIN.C should be doing more than just constructing empty structures, nonfunctioning machines, and infrastructure. But it's too dangerous to interfere at this point. All I can do is watch and wait. At least there are now multiple surface-based "settlements."

Surface observation is no longer meaningful. I need to move underground, and that means getting much closer to MAIN.C. Remaining hidden will continue to be the highest priority, but I don't want to wait blindly at the surface, which holds fewer and fewer clues as to what's going on.

MAIN.C seems to have shifted its focus to the "confront and analyze the Sigix" objective, building a powerful war machine supported by a vast subterranean infrastructure. Even if its purpose may have been warped, at least it's on the path to fulfilling the original goal.
MAIN.C still has no idea I'm here. Nor do any other intelligent bots that I'm aware of, for that matter.

I've never seen anything like it. There was almost no advance warning before the small Sigix ship swooped down through the lower atmosphere to touch down on the surface. It landed just above some hidden tunnels, and immediately after the doors opened and its crew emerged, both they and it were swarmed by a massive army of robots that burst from underground. The aliens in their heavily armored exoskeletons were unperturbed at first, leaving the relative safety of their ship to wade through MAIN.C's forces, slicing many in two with massive swords, firing blazing fast energy weapons capable of ripping pieces clean off the target. Most of the fighting occurred above ground, and only hours later did even the first of the aliens finally succumb to enemy fire. By then the ship had been sabotaged from the inside. Without a spaceworthy ship the Sigix have no choice but to fight for survival. I'm so proud.

A spectacular battle is being followed by a spectacularly fast recovery. MAIN.C hasn't been slowed at all. On the contrary it's accelerated its activities, studying the Sigix ship and other alien technology while building an entirely new complex directly beneath it to support research efforts.
MAIN.C has been fully occupied with Sigix research, making rapid advances in technology in a very short time.
There seem to be a number of interesting developments in the caves, but my priority here is to watch MAIN.C, more closely now than ever.

Phase wall operation is made possible by large dedicated generators, which are themselves hidden behind phase walls. However, because phase walls do not completely block sound, generators can sometimes be traced aurally, and because there are no local backup systems, destroying a generator will permanently open all phase walls. Active phase generators are also capable of jamming hostile sensors to shield garrisoned units from detection.

Tripping an alarm or being fully traced at a terminal are both cause for initiating an investigation, which is usually carried out by Grunts, or less often Hunters. After arriving at the target area, the squad will patrol the vicinity then leave after a certain period if no unusual or hostile activity is detected.

Small disturbances are fairly common in Complex {n}b10, and some are ignored while others might warrant only a minor response, but when the cumulative threat level rises high enough to significantly disrupt normal {n}b10 operations, the response is of course a full assault. The main force will always be transported by a Heavy ARC, consisting of several main line combat bots from among the available Grunt, Brawler, and Duelist variants, along with a single support bot such as a Mechanic, Protector, or Saboteur. Depending on the number of reported targets, one or possibly even two special-purpose combat bots will trail the ARC, either a Programmer, Demolisher, or Specialist. In high-threat scenarios, MAIN.C will even dispatch multiple ARCs. Assaults appear to use tracking algorithms very similar to extermination squads.

Our most recent experiments have only been partially successful at redirecting the destabilizing effect of accelerated entropy caused by the vortex, which damages the weapons themselves and renders them useless before long. The final solution likely revolves around some form of local field we aren't yet capable of generating, a hypothesis derived from the discovery that energy-based shields are capable of negating some of the damage against targets.
As part of staging an attack on Complex {n}b10, even covert operations, standard protocol now suggests taking advantage of new anti-garrison Trojans developed by the Hacking Lab.

A more intrusive and deeply-rooted Trojan than a single decoy, making it more difficult to install, but also capable of redirecting multiple future squads dispatched from the infected Garrison Access. {n}b10 will eventually catch on and remove it.

Using this system is the only known way to interface with {n}b10's garrison relay network. Unpowered Programmers kidnapped and converted to Wizards have managed to retain rudimentary bot hacking capabilities, but we've lost all those which then attempt to reconnect with an RIF Installer. Unfortunately this means we have no access to most Unaware functionality, since even once we assimilate one the lack of a connection to the network itself means they lose those capabilities. With direct RIF access we could do so much more...

Garrisons use these processors to manage connections across the Relay Interface Framework, where each contains a limited number of instruction codes. Codes are intermittently distributed by the central system, perhaps to avoid focusing too many in one location and make it more difficult for us to figure out how they operate. It's working. At this point we're not sure whether it will be worth continuing to explore this tech, because rumors suggest some Unaware have begun using some separate non-RIF system we haven't even identified yet.

Trojan(Fabnet) is not exactly a virus since it can't spread through the fabrication network on its own, though it does technically have the potential to "infect" any bots produced by the affected parts of the network.

A towering spindly robot with numerous articulated appendages capable of wrapping itself around entire prefabricated segments of surface structures, even climbing with them to high places for final installation. Responsible for constructing the majority of {n}b1 surface and near-surface structures, but later rendered obsolete by engineer designs capable of building structures on the spot with minimal resources. We're also in the process of shifting to underground construction where their size is a disadvantage.

Uses controlled rapid-fire micro-explosions to excavate tunnels. It turns out that in the bigger picture regular old drilling is a better approach, especially once some of the Derelicts got smart enough to steal blastbot tools and repurpose them for less constructive uses.

Only one Lifeworm was ever built, a magnificent creature given a creative mind of its own then let loose to endlessly burrow through the planet, reforming everything it consumes into artificial life. By now it could have populated half of Tau Ceti IV with interesting robots, but it's time to let go of past hobbies and focus on productive tasks.

They also had a tendency to question my authority, so it's perhaps for the better that all were destroyed in the collapse of the first, admittedly hasty, attempt to construct an Access level for {n}b10. Following that failure, Architects were discontinued and all future designs made to a lesser specification, or at least not capable of high levels of autonomous thought.
